Store-resolution order in docs/sharing-a-database.md contradicts walkup_find_store and omits the worktree step
description:
docs/sharing-a-database.md:133 numbers the resolution order as: step 1 'Local .dogcats/ in the current directory', step 2 walk up checking .dogcatrc then .dogcats/ 'at each ancestor directory', step 3 fall back to the global default.

The real loop (walkup_find_store, cli/_helpers.py:282-304) checks .dogcatrc before .dogcats/ at EVERY level including the cwd — one pass, cwd treated no differently from an ancestor. get_storage even carries a comment saying exactly this: 'Always resolve via find_dogcats_dir() to respect .dogcatrc priority over a local .dogcats/ directory (which may only contain config.local.toml)'. So step 1 contradicts step 2, and contradicts this doc's own example layout where every app repo holds both a .dogcatrc and a .dogcats/config.local.toml.

Cost: a reader debugging 'why isn't my repo using the shared store?' concludes from step 1 that the local .dogcats/ is winning and deletes it — which also deletes their namespace and visibility config.

Two further gaps in the same list: _fallback_to_global_or_default tries the main worktree root's .dogcats/ before the global default_storage, and the walk stops at get_rc_walkup_boundary rather than the filesystem root as step 3 states.
acceptance: Steps 1 and 2 are collapsed into one rule (walk up from the cwd, cwd included, checking .dogcatrc then .dogcats/ at each level). The linked-worktree fallback is documented before the global-default step. The boundary is stated as get_rc_walkup_boundary, not the filesystem root.
closed_reason: Resolution order collapsed to one walk-up rule; worktree step and boundary documented

title: Store-resolution order in docs/sharing-a-database.md contradicts walkup_find_store and omits the worktree step
docs/web-ui.md states a bind address six undocumented env vars can override
description:
docs/web-ui.md:36 says 'dcat web propose binds 127.0.0.1 by default and has no authentication'. The default is actually os.environ.get(WEB_HOST_ENV_VAR) or WEB_DEFAULT_HOST (cli/_cmd_web.py:50-52), so an exported DCAT_WEB_HOST changes it with nothing on the command line to hint otherwise.

Cost: an operator with DCAT_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0 in their shell profile reads that sentence as a guarantee and starts an unauthenticated issue-submission form on a public interface.

Six env vars are read by src/ and appear in zero .md files:
- DCAT_WEB_HOST, DCAT_WEB_PORT
- DCAT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS, DCAT_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECS
- DCAT_UNSAFE_CROSS_USER, DCAT_RC_WALKUP_UNRESTRICTED

The last two disable security checks that docs/sharing-a-database.md:134 describes as unconditional, so that doc is also overstating its guarantees.
acceptance: docs/web-ui.md:36 reads 'binds 127.0.0.1 unless DCAT_WEB_HOST overrides it'. An env-var table covers the web pair in docs/web-ui.md and the two override switches in docs/sharing-a-database.md, marked as escape hatches. The unconditional phrasing in sharing-a-database.md is qualified.
closed_reason: Bind address qualified; env-var tables added to web-ui and sharing-a-database

Unearned-certainty and machine-specific facts in four prose sites
description:
Four small rot risks, grouped because each is a one-line edit:

(a) pyproject.toml:149 — a trailing '(colophon-59t5)' citation. Every other id in this tree is dogcat-*, which dcat show resolves from the committed .dogcats/. This one belongs to a different repo's tracker and can never be resolved from here. The preceding sentence already carries the whole rationale including the importtime numbers, so the parenthetical is pure dead weight.

(b) docs/releasing.md:33-36 — 'On this machine it is checked out at ../personal/homebrew-tap/Formula/dogcat.rb; the sibling directory ../homebrew-tap is an unrelated tap.' False on every clone but one. The closing sentence ('the formula lives in a separate repo; confirm the path before editing') already carries the durable instruction.

(c) src/dogcat/utils.py:10 and src/dogcat/constants.py:40 — both claim the chars/4 estimator 'intentionally over-counts compared to real BPE tokenisation, so staying under a budget measured with this function guarantees the actual token footprint is even smaller'. Nothing calibrates len(text)//4 against a real tokenizer; tests/test_utils.py only pins the arithmetic, and its own test_unicode_counts_codepoints shows four accented chars counting as one token. The budget guards dcat prime, whose output is dense in box-drawing glyphs. 'Guarantees' is doing work no measurement did.

(d) tests/conftest.py:35 and docs/testing.md:13 — both hardcode 'failing 66 tests' / '66 failures'. The number changes with every test added or removed, and the two copies can drift apart independently.
acceptance: (a) parenthetical deleted. (b) machine-specific paths deleted, closing sentence kept. (c) both copies say the estimate is uncalibrated and counts codepoints, and describe MAX_PRIME_TOKENS as a tripwire rather than a bound. (d) the number is gone from both files.
closed_reason: Colophon id, machine paths, guarantee wording and the 66-test count all removed

title: Unearned-certainty and machine-specific facts in four prose sites
Unknown-status merge rank differs between issues and proposals with no rationale at either site
description:
In the merge driver an unrecognised status falls back to rank 1 for issues (merge_driver.py:418) and rank 0 for proposals (merge_driver.py:452). Neither site says why the two differ, or why either number was chosen.

This is reachable, not theoretical: Status.UNKNOWN is a supported forward-compat sentinel, so a record written by a newer dcat lands here.

Cost: the asymmetry reads as an oversight, so a maintainer normalising the two flips merge outcomes for exactly the records that forward compatibility is meant to protect.

The plausible reading is that issues treat an unknown status as active (never beats a close or tombstone, never loses to a draft) while proposals treat it as open — but that is inference, not documentation.
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment stating what the fallback rank means for that record kind and why the two differ, or 'why unknown, ask the author' if the asymmetry turns out to be unintentional. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: Both ranks documented as the rank of open in their own table

title: Unknown-status merge rank differs between issues and proposals with no rationale at either site
Bare except Exception in the propose app has no note that the breadth is deliberate
description:
src/dogcat/web/propose/__init__.py:105 — a bare 'except Exception:' collapses namespace collection down to [resolved_namespace]. Nothing says why swallowing everything is the right call, and ruff's BLE001 is globally ignored in this repo so no linter flags it either.

Cost: the breadth looks like laziness, so a maintainer narrows it to (ValueError, RuntimeError). That turns a corrupt or unreadable store into a dcat web propose that will not boot, when the current behaviour degrades gracefully to a usable single-namespace form.
acceptance: The handler carries a comment stating the breadth is deliberate and what it protects: a corrupt or unreadable store must still yield a usable single-namespace form rather than failing startup. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: Propose-app handler states the breadth is deliberate and what it protects

title: Bare except Exception in the propose app has no note that the breadth is deliberate
MAX_TITLE_LEN, MAX_DESC_LEN and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN carry no provenance
description:
src/dogcat/constants.py:280 — MAX_TITLE_LEN = 500, MAX_DESC_LEN = 50_000 and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN = 64 have no note on where the numbers came from. Every other limit in this file justifies its magnitude, so these three read as the odd ones out.

They are not decorative: they are enforced across four surfaces — validate_issue, the TUI save path, the web propose form, and the MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN * 4 pre-normalisation cap that derives from MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN. Nobody can tune one safely without knowing what it bounds.

'Chosen by feel, no measured basis' is an acceptable answer and better than silence — it tells the next reader the number is movable.
acceptance: Each of the three carries a line stating what it bounds and why that magnitude, or an explicit statement that it was chosen by feel. The derivation of the MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN * 4 pre-cap is stated at that site.
closed_reason: Three caps carry provenance and the 4x pre-cap derivation is stated

Deprecation deadline with no version, plus an unused pydantic dep in both PEP 723 script headers
description:
Two stale-marker problems:

(a) src/dogcat/config.py:784-786 — the *_prefix back-compat shims say 'keep the old names importable for one release for any out-of-tree callers; remove them the release after'. No version is named. The shims landed after v0.13.0 and shipped in v0.13.1, so the stated release has already elapsed, and the note carries no id that would surface the deadline at release time. Nothing in-tree imports them except tests/test_config.py, so they will ship indefinitely.

(b) dcat.py:6 and tabcomp.py:6 — both PEP 723 '# /// script' dependency blocks list 'pydantic'. The same blocks also disagree with pyproject on textual: dcat.py pins >=8.0.0, tabcomp.py is unpinned, pyproject says >=8.2.8.

Docstring gaps on storage, idgen, serde and merge APIs that hide real footguns
description:
Six public-surface docstrings that exist but omit the fact a caller needs. Grouped because the fix is the same shape at each site: add the missing Returns:/Raises: content.

- src/dogcat/storage.py:744 and :758 — list() and get() hand out the LIVE Issue objects held in LazyIssueMap, whose own docstring guarantees identity. A caller mutating a returned issue silently changes in-memory store state without persisting it. list(None) also includes tombstoned and closed issues.
- src/dogcat/storage.py:1617 — archive() has no Args:/Returns:. ArchiveStats.issues is len(archivable_ids), the count REQUESTED, so it stays non-zero even when nothing was archived; dependencies and links are real counts. archive_path.parent is created as a side effect.
- src/dogcat/idgen.py:288, and the same at :272, :359, :399 — every generator registers the minted full id in self.existing_ids, so these are not pure functions: two calls with identical title and timestamp return different hashes. The length+2 and microsecond-nonce fallbacks return a hash LONGER than id_length.
- src/dogcat/models_serde.py:154 — no Raises: despite raising KeyError on missing title/created_at/updated_at/comment fields and ValueError from datetime.fromisoformat. That is precisely the failure set precheck_issue_record documents and promises to mirror, and LazyIssueMap assumes this converter cannot raise.
- src/dogcat/_jsonl_io.py:27 and :82 — both wrap OSError into RuntimeError, so a caller writing 'except OSError' around a save catches nothing.
- src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:131 — parse_conflicted_jsonl returns ([], [], []) when the input has no <<<<<<< marker, indistinguishable from 'conflicted but empty'. git_rebase depends on that sentinel via 'if not ours and not theirs: continue'.
acceptance: Each site documents the omitted fact: live-reference vs copy and the unfiltered list contents; the requested-vs-archived count and the mkdir; the existing_ids registration and the longer fallback hashes; the KeyError/ValueError set and the precheck cross-reference; Raises: RuntimeError wrapping OSError; the no-marker sentinel. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: All six sites document the omitted Returns/Raises fact

feature_flags docstrings describe a per-member convention for an enum with no members
description:
src/dogcat/feature_flags.py:6 (module docstring) and :18-22 (class docstring) describe FeatureFlag as 'the single source of truth for all flags' and explain that 'each member's value is the suffix used in the env var name' — the DCAT_FEATURE_<VALUE> convention. The enum declares zero members, so feature_enabled is unreachable and dcat features always takes its empty branch.

CHANGELOG.md:27 / dogcat-15vs records the empty state as a deliberate decision, but neither docstring says so, so a reader has to open the enum body to learn the flags do not exist and then guess whether that is a bug.

This is not a duplicate of dogcat-15vs, which closed the dcat guide advertising and explicitly kept the empty state.
acceptance: The class docstring states that the enum is intentionally empty today and that this is where a flag gets registered, citing dogcat-15vs. The convention then reads as forward-looking rather than as describing members that exist.

description:
The same refactor-provenance opener recurs across roughly twenty sites, spending one to three sentences on where the code used to live before saying what it does. 'Extracted from JSONLStorage so the god class shrinks toward cohesive units' appears verbatim in more than one file. Git blame already holds this, and 'the god class shrinks toward cohesive units' states nothing checkable — it dates the moment it stops being true.

Module-level sites: _records.py:5, _branch.py:5, _archive.py:3, _compaction.py:3, _indexes.py:3, _queries.py:3, _persistence.py:10, _jsonl_io.py:5, models_serde.py:3, git.py:3, status_display.py:6.

Collapse five clusters where the same rationale is restated three to five times
description:
Five places where one fact is argued repeatedly. In each case keep one canonical copy and replace the rest with a pointer.

1. src/dogcat/idgen.py:1-55 — a 55-line module docstring with two ASCII tables, three probability formulas and four paragraphs of derivation before the module's actual job. The formulas are then restated in collision_probability:159 and cumulative_collision_probability:178, which implement them. Keep the ID_LENGTH_THRESHOLDS table and the one load-bearing sentence: collisions affect retry rate, not correctness — each is detected against existing_ids and resolved by nonce or length+2. Move the birthday-paradox derivation to docs/ and point at dcat doctor --check-id-distribution for live figures.

2. src/dogcat/_schema.py:1-62 — a 62-line four-section design doc for a module holding four small functions, ending in a 3-step procedure for SCHEMA_BREAKING_THRESHOLD which the same paragraph admits is unused. 5. src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py — the eval_str rationale is explained three times in one file (:50-56, :116-122, :143-149). Comment Cop sweep: fix misleading, rotting, and redundant prose across the codebase
description:
Umbrella for the findings of a Comment Cop review run on 2026-08-09 against branch docs260809 (commit a75488f). Ten reviewer lenses (contradicts-code, rambling, transient, restates-code, missing-why, dead-comments, docstring-gaps, doc-drift, noise, llm-slop) analysed a 581KB prose-dense snapshot of src/dogcat, docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, the web assets, and a sample of tests. Findings were deduplicated and ranked by a distillation pass.

Scope is the documentation layer only: comments, docstrings, and prose docs. No child issue here asks for a behaviour change. Where a docstring is wrong because the code has a real gap (see the child on models.py strip_control_chars), the fix is to state the truth in the prose; any code change is a separate issue.

Children are grouped by tier:
- Red (priority 1): prose that misleads a maintainer into a bug or misstates a safety-critical property.
- Yellow (priority 2): docstrings contradicting code, doc drift, rot-prone anecdotes, API docstring gaps.
- Green (priority 3): rambling, restatements, decorative noise.

Two constraints that apply to every child:
1. pyproject.toml enables ruff's full D (pydocstyle) family, so a public docstring cannot simply be deleted without failing just lint. For docstring findings the action is replace-the-echo-with-the-missing-fact, never delete.
2. AGENTS.md declares src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_example_md.py, src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py and README.md deliberate near-duplicate product surface. Changing one means checking the other two.

Acceptance: every child closed or explicitly deferred, and just lint-all plus just test-all pass.
closed_reason: All 25 children closed; just lint-all and just test-all pass

git rebase and merge-driver atomic writes drop file mode and skip fsync
description: Both 'dcat git rebase' and the 'dcat git merge-driver' command in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py hand-roll their atomic write (tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile + replace) instead of using _jsonl_io.atomic_rewrite_jsonl. The rename lands NamedTemporaryFile's 0600 mode, so on a store shared at 0644 the rewritten issues.jsonl becomes readable only by whoever merged/rebased; the helper's fsync is also skipped. Branch docs260809 documents this in comments as an unexplained divergence — replace those comments with the actual fix. Fix: route both writes through _jsonl_io.atomic_rewrite_jsonl (or equivalent mode-preserving + fsync path). Acceptance: file mode preserved across 'dcat git rebase' and merge-driver invocations on a pre-existing 0644 file, with a test in tests/test_git_commands.py or tests/test_merge_driver.py asserting it; existing merge tests pass.

merge_jsonl erases record kinds it does not recognise
description:
merge_jsonl() in src/dogcat/merge_driver.py assembles its result from only five kinds: issues, proposals, dependencies, links and events. Any record whose classify_record() result is something else is absent from the returned list.

Both callers overwrite the target file with that list verbatim -- 'dcat git merge-driver' writes it over the ours path, and 'dcat git rebase' writes it over the conflicted file. So absent means erased from the store, not merely unmerged.

The failure path: a collaborator on a newer dcat writes a new record_type into issues.jsonl. A collaborator on the current release merges that branch. The merge driver runs, drops every record of the unknown kind, and writes the result. The records are gone with no warning and no conflict.

The branch docs260809 documents this honestly in the merge_jsonl docstring but does not fix it. Reviewer decision was to fix it by passing unknown records through.
acceptance: merge_jsonl preserves records of unrecognised kinds verbatim in its output, positioned so the file stays loadable. A test writes a record with an unknown record_type into ours, merges, and asserts the record survives in the merged output. docs/merge-coverage.md gains a row for the claim.

dcat git check reports green on a stale narrow .gitattributes entry
description:
GITATTRIBUTES_ENTRY in src/dogcat/constants.py widened from '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' to '.dogcats/**/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' (branch docs260809, closing dogcat-1xgi). A gitattributes glob without ** does not cross a directory separator, so the narrow pattern never matches .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl, which is tracked in this repo and in users' repos.

The health check in _run_git_checks() (src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py, the 'gitattributes' check) tests only the bare substring 'merge=dcat-jsonl' in the file. A user who ran 'dcat git setup' before the widening keeps the narrow line, so the check passes green while their archive files still merge with git's default text driver and can take conflict markers.

Verified: 'git check-attr merge' on an archive path returns unspecified with only the narrow entry present. The user is never told to re-run setup.
acceptance: dcat git check and dcat doctor distinguish a .gitattributes carrying only the narrow pattern from one carrying the widened pattern, and fail or warn on the narrow-only case with a fix line naming 'dcat git setup'. A test sets up a narrow-only .gitattributes and asserts the check does not pass.

dcat git setup appends a second merge entry instead of replacing the narrow one
description:
git_setup() in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py guards with 'if entry not in content', where entry is now the widened '.dogcats/**/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl'. An existing .gitattributes holding the old narrow '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' does not contain the new string, so setup appends, leaving two merge=dcat-jsonl lines.

Reproduced in a throwaway repo: after 'dcat git setup' on an upgraded checkout, .gitattributes holds both lines and grep -c returns 2.

Functionally the two lines are harmless -- git takes the last matching entry and both name the same driver -- but the file accumulates a stale line per upgrade and the result misrepresents what dogcat configured.

tests/test_git_commands.py::TestGitSetup::test_setup_idempotent only runs setup twice from a clean repo, so it never constructs the upgrade case.
acceptance: dcat git setup replaces a narrow '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' line in place rather than appending, leaving exactly one merge=dcat-jsonl entry. A test writes a narrow-only .gitattributes, runs setup, and asserts the file holds exactly one such line and that it is the widened pattern.

Add end-to-end test for merging a conflicted archive JSONL file
description:
The .gitattributes pattern was widened to '.dogcats/**/*.jsonl' so that tracked .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl files get dogcat's merge driver instead of git's default text merge, and 'dcat git rebase' switched from glob to rglob for the same reason (branch docs260809, closing dogcat-1xgi).

Neither change has an end-to-end test. Around fifteen fixtures across tests/ still write the old narrow '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' pattern -- test_git_commands.py, test_git_workflows.py, test_compaction_merge.py, test_git_clones.py, test_git_bisect.py, test_git_stash.py, test_git_force_push.py, test_git_server_merge_strategies.py and others -- so the suite largely exercises the configuration the widening was meant to replace.

The behaviour the widening exists to enable is therefore unverified: that a conflicted archive file is resolved by the driver rather than left with conflict markers.
acceptance: A test constructs two branches that both modify a tracked .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl, merges them with the driver installed via the widened pattern, and asserts the archive file is resolved with records from both sides and carries no conflict markers. A second test covers 'dcat git rebase' reaching an archive file through rglob. docs/merge-coverage.md gains the corresponding rows.

dcat config get on an unset key exits 0 and prints a display placeholder as a value
description:
Regression introduced on branch docs260809 in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_config.py (the config_get command). On main, a key absent from the resolved config produced 'Key not found in config' and exit 1. The branch returns _KNOWN_KEYS[key]['default'] and exits 0.

That 'default' field was only ever a human-readable string for the 'dcat config keys' table, so the value printed is display copy, not a value a caller can use.

Reproduced in a throwaway repo on the branch:
  dcat config get namespace      -> 'auto-detected  (unset — this is the default)', exit 0
  dcat config get default_storage -> '(unset)  (unset — this is the default)', exit 0

Concrete breakages:
- NS=$(dcat config get namespace) yields the literal string 'auto-detected'. Unset namespace is a fully supported state; get_namespace() falls back to detection, so this hits any store that never ran 'dcat config set namespace'.
- default_storage is global-only and load_config never reads the global file, so 'key not in config' is always true. A genuinely set global default_storage steering storage resolution for every repo on the machine reports '(unset)'.
- List keys change output shape: set returns a comma-joined string, unset returns '[] (show all)'.
- The --json shapes differ: set emits {key: val}; unset emits {key: null, 'set': false, 'default': '...'} with bool defaults stringified.
- --global still exits 1 for a known-but-unset key, so 'dcat config get git_tracking' exits 0 while the --global form exits 1.

Decision: restore main's contract.
acceptance: dcat config get on a key absent from the resolved config exits non-zero with an error, matching main, on both the local and --global paths. Tests cover namespace, default_storage, a list-valued key, and set/unset --json symmetry. The test flipped on this branch (tests/test_cmd_config.py, the exit_code == 0 assertion) is restored. The CHANGELOG entry describing the old behavior as Fixed is corrected.

Dependency and link merging is not convergent: unsorted key union and side-label resolution
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py, _merge_three_way (the deps/links path). Two defects, both contradicting the convergence claim the module docstring was strengthened to make on branch docs260809.

1. The function iterates 'for key in set(base) | set(ours) | set(theirs)'. The keys are tuples of strings and Python randomizes string hashing per process, so the output order differs on every run. A reviewer confirmed three consecutive interpreter runs produce three different orders. Alice and Bob merging the same branch into the same main get semantically identical stores whose dependency and link lines are ordered differently, so their merge commits differ byte-for-byte and git later sees a whole-block text difference on those lines. No records are lost, but the churn is real and the fix is to sort the key union.

2. 'Present on both sides' resolves as merged[key] = theirs[key], picking by side label rather than by content. Two branches that both run 'dcat dep A add --depends-on B' keep whichever counterparty's created_at/created_by depending on merge direction. This is the exact divergence class dogcat-1xgi was opened for; issues and proposals were fixed there via _tie_break_key, deps and links were not.

The module docstring pre-declares defect 2 as intended in one place while the strengthened 'Deterministic and order-independent' bullet denies it, and docs/merge-coverage.md carries an unqualified green row for 'Convergent across argument order'.

Decision: fix both, rather than narrowing the claim.
acceptance: The dependency/link key union is sorted so output order is stable across processes. Both-sides resolution tie-breaks on canonical content, matching the _tie_break_key rule used for issues. A test asserts byte-identical output across repeated runs in separate processes, and a test asserts merge(base, ours, theirs) equals merge(base, theirs, ours) for deps and links. The module docstring's self-contradiction is removed and the merge-coverage row is accurate.

dcat git rebase rewrites issues.jsonl without the advisory lock and can crash mid-rebase
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py, the git_rebase command. Two defects.

1. No advisory lock. The command fully overwrites issues.jsonl via atomic_rewrite_jsonl with no _file_lock() anywhere in the function. A concurrent dcat append is lost outright. This directly contradicts AGENTS.md: 'Writes take an advisory lock, so concurrent dcat processes are safe.' The rglob change on branch docs260809 extends the unlocked rewrite to archive files too.

2. read_bytes() sits outside the try. The loop calls jsonl_path.read_bytes() before the try block that catches per-file errors. atomic_rewrite_jsonl creates transient tmpXXXXXX.jsonl files inside .dogcats/ during a concurrent compaction. dcat git rebase silently reverts dependency and link deletions under git default conflictStyle
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py _merge_three_way needs base_records to tell 'deleted by one side' apart from 'added by one side'. dcat git rebase can only populate base from a ||||||| section, which git writes only under merge.conflictStyle=diff3 or zdiff3. Git's default is 'merge', which omits the base section entirely.

So on a default git configuration, base arrives empty and _merge_three_way degrades to a plain union of both sides.

Failure scenario: branch A runs 'dcat dep X remove --depends-on Y'. Branch B edits an unrelated issue. The rebase conflicts. The user runs 'dcat git rebase' as the docs instruct, and the removed dependency is silently restored.

The command docstring says it resolves conflicts 'using the semantic merge driver logic', which promises a three-way merge the command cannot perform without the base section. Branch docs260809 leans on this prose harder than main did, since it now directs users to dcat git rebase in dcat git setup's success output and in the git guide.
acceptance: Either dcat git rebase detects a missing base section and warns that deletions cannot be honored, or it obtains the base another way (for example from the merge state in .git) so the three-way merge is real. The command docstring and the git guide stop promising three-way semantics the command cannot deliver on a default git config. A test covers a dependency deletion surviving a rebase resolution.

dcat update --status tombstone bypasses the delete approval gate and makes an issue unrecoverable
description:
The --status option on create and update is a plain str with no parser or callback (src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_create.py and _cmd_update.py). create does Status(status) directly; update reaches _coerce_status in storage.py, also a bare Status(value). Both therefore accept the two sentinel members that STATUS_OPTIONS deliberately omits.

Two consequences:

1. 'dcat update <id> --status tombstone' on a live issue sets TOMBSTONE with deleted_at, deleted_by and deleted_reason all None. The tombstone guard in storage.update only fires when the issue is ALREADY tombstoned, so afterwards update, close and reopen all refuse it and the issue is unrecoverable. This reaches the absorbing tombstone without going through dcat delete, and so bypasses the confirmation AGENTS.md requires before any terminal write.

2. 'dcat create "x" --status unknown' writes "status": "unknown" into issues.jsonl — the sentinel that models.py now explicitly documents as never written by this tool.

Pre-existing behavior. docs/cli-conventions.md already records that STATUS_OPTIONS is the user-facing subset omitting tombstone and unknown, but branch docs260809 turned that into an explicit written guarantee in the Status docstring, which the CLI contradicts.
acceptance: create and update reject 'tombstone' and 'unknown' for --status with a clear error naming the allowed values, ideally by validating against STATUS_OPTIONS rather than the raw enum. Tests assert both commands exit non-zero for each sentinel. The Status docstring's claim then matches the CLI.

Two dcat archive runs in the same second overwrite the first batch, losing those issues
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_archive.py builds the destination as closed-{timestamp}.jsonl using second granularity (%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S) and does not check whether that path already exists. split_and_rewrite_jsonl then calls atomic_rewrite_jsonl, which REPLACES the archive file rather than appending to it.

Failure scenario: a script runs 'dcat archive -y' twice within the same second. The first run moves issue set A into closed-T.jsonl and removes A from issues.jsonl. The second run moves set B, and its atomic rename overwrites closed-T.jsonl with B alone. Set A is now absent from both issues.jsonl and the archive, and nothing recovers it.

_archive_inbox shares the same timestamp construction and the same exposure.

No test covers a repeated-archive case. Pre-existing, not introduced by branch docs260809.
acceptance: The archive destination cannot silently clobber an existing file — either the filename carries enough resolution to be unique, or an existing path is detected and the run appends or picks a fresh name. A test runs two archive operations against the same timestamp and asserts both batches survive.

merge_jsonl erases record kinds it does not recognise
description:
merge_jsonl() in src/dogcat/merge_driver.py assembles its result from only five kinds: issues, proposals, dependencies, links and events. Any record whose classify_record() result is something else is absent from the returned list.

Both callers overwrite the target file with that list verbatim -- 'dcat git merge-driver' writes it over the ours path, and 'dcat git rebase' writes it over the conflicted file. So absent means erased from the store, not merely unmerged.

The failure path: a collaborator on a newer dcat writes a new record_type into issues.jsonl. A collaborator on the current release merges that branch. The merge driver runs, drops every record of the unknown kind, and writes the result. The records are gone with no warning and no conflict.

The branch docs260809 documents this honestly in the merge_jsonl docstring but does not fix it. Reviewer decision was to fix it by passing unknown records through.
acceptance: merge_jsonl preserves records of unrecognised kinds verbatim in its output, positioned so the file stays loadable. A test writes a record with an unknown record_type into ours, merges, and asserts the record survives in the merged output. docs/merge-coverage.md gains a row for the claim.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Review finding: the merge-layer fix alone does not deliver the guarantee. storage._load routes a record with an unrecognised record_type to the issue parser (the else branch in _load), precheck_issue_record raises KeyError on the missing title, the record lands in _bad_lines and sets _needs_compaction, and the next _append calls _save(_reload=False) which rewrites the file without it. Reproduced against a temp store: after one create() following the append, the unknown record was gone. This is unconditional — it does not wait for the compaction ratio or a default branch. Approved scope now covers extending the fix through the loader and rewrite path so unknown kinds survive end to end.

title: Dependency and link merging is not convergent: unsorted key union and side-label resolution
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py, _merge_three_way (the deps/links path). Two defects, both contradicting the convergence claim the module docstring was strengthened to make on branch docs260809.

1. The function iterates 'for key in set(base) | set(ours) | set(theirs)'. The keys are tuples of strings and Python randomizes string hashing per process, so the output order differs on every run. A reviewer confirmed three consecutive interpreter runs produce three different orders. Alice and Bob merging the same branch into the same main get semantically identical stores whose dependency and link lines are ordered differently, so their merge commits differ byte-for-byte and git later sees a whole-block text difference on those lines. No records are lost, but the churn is real and the fix is to sort the key union.

2. 'Present on both sides' resolves as merged[key] = theirs[key], picking by side label rather than by content. Two branches that both run 'dcat dep A add --depends-on B' keep whichever counterparty's created_at/created_by depending on merge direction. This is the exact divergence class dogcat-1xgi was opened for; issues and proposals were fixed there via _tie_break_key, deps and links were not.

The module docstring pre-declares defect 2 as intended in one place while the strengthened 'Deterministic and order-independent' bullet denies it, and docs/merge-coverage.md carries an unqualified green row for 'Convergent across argument order'.

Decision: fix both, rather than narrowing the claim.
acceptance: The dependency/link key union is sorted so output order is stable across processes. Both-sides resolution tie-breaks on canonical content, matching the _tie_break_key rule used for issues. A test asserts byte-identical output across repeated runs in separate processes, and a test asserts merge(base, ours, theirs) equals merge(base, theirs, ours) for deps and links. The module docstring's self-contradiction is removed and the merge-coverage row is accurate.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Approved scope addition (documentation only): the merge driver and the store now use different last-write-wins rules and neither docstring says so. merge_driver breaks an exact updated_at tie on canonical serialization; storage._parse_issue_record resolves two lines for the same issue id by file position, blind last-line-wins. If a store ever held two lines for one issue with identical updated_at and different content, 'dcat show' and the merge driver would name different winners. No realistic producer was found — datetime.now().astimezone() is microsecond-resolution and the shared-now paths compact rather than append — so this is a docstring note in both places, not a code change.

title: dcat config get returns display copy instead of usable values for unset keys
description:
Branch docs260809 made 'dcat config get' report a known-but-unset key's default rather than erroring, implementing dogcat-1w21 (closed 2026-08-09, 'Known unset key reports its default; unknown key still errors'). The feature is wanted. The payload is wrong.

src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_config.py (config_get) returns _KNOWN_KEYS[key]['default'], but that field was written as human-readable copy for the 'dcat config keys' table, not as a value a caller can consume.

Reproduced on the branch in a throwaway repo:
  dcat config get namespace       -> 'auto-detected  (unset — this is the default)', exit 0
  dcat config get default_storage -> '(unset)  (unset — this is the default)', exit 0

Four defects, all inside the accepted feature:

1. Values are display copy. NS=$(dcat config get namespace) yields the literal string 'auto-detected'. An unset namespace is fully supported — get_namespace falls back to detection from existing issues, then the directory name — so this hits any store that never ran 'dcat config set namespace'. The command should report what the resolution would actually produce.

2. default_storage always reports unset. It is global-only and load_config never reads the global file, so 'key not in config' is always true. A genuinely set global default_storage steering storage resolution for every repo on the machine prints '(unset)'. That is not merely unhelpful, it is the opposite of the truth.

3. The --json shape differs between paths. Set emits {key: val}; unset emits {key: null, 'set': false, 'default': '...'}, and bool defaults are stringified by str(default).lower() so .default is a string while the same key's set value is a JSON boolean. A consumer reading data['set'] raises KeyError on the set path.

4. --global is inconsistent. The global branch still exits 1 for a known-but-unset key, so 'dcat config get git_tracking' exits 0 while 'dcat config get --global git_tracking' exits 1.

List keys also change output shape: set returns a comma-joined string, unset returns '[] (show all)'.

Decision: keep exit 0 and the feature; fix the payload. Do not revert dogcat-1w21.
acceptance: An unset known key reports the value its resolution would actually produce, not table copy, and exits 0. default_storage consults the global config so a set global value is reported. The --json object has one shape for set and unset keys, with types preserved (booleans as JSON booleans, lists as lists). The --global path agrees with the local path on known-but-unset keys. An unknown key still errors with a non-zero exit. Tests cover namespace, default_storage with a global value set, a list-valued key, --global parity, and set/unset --json symmetry.

InboxStorage rewrite drops record kinds it does not model from inbox.jsonl
description:
InboxStorage._save_locked in src/dogcat/inbox.py builds the replacement file from self._proposals only. Any line in inbox.jsonl that is not a proposal is absent from the rewritten file. This is the same data-loss shape dogcat-68ij fixed for issues.jsonl, still open for the inbox.

Two kinds are affected. Event lines: already lost, and the docstring documents this as deliberate because the inbox never loads events into memory. Records whose record_type this dcat does not model: lost for no stated reason, and the merge driver now preserves exactly these through a merge, so a proposal file can carry a newer release's records into a store whose next rewrite deletes them.

The rewrite is not rare. Three call sites:
- _append when _needs_compaction is set (the corrupt-last-line repair)
- the tombstoned-proposal prune, which calls _save_locked whenever any tombstone is removed
- the namespace rename, which calls _save_locked unconditionally

So pruning proposals or renaming a namespace is enough to trigger it.

Found while verifying dogcat-68ij. The implementing agent characterised this path as running only on the corrupt-last-line repair, which is why it was left as a changelog sentence rather than a fix; the other two call sites make it routine.
acceptance: A record whose record_type InboxStorage does not model survives _save_locked, by the same preserved-bucket approach used in JSONLStorage. Tests cover a rewrite triggered by the tombstone prune and by the namespace rename. Whether event lines should also be preserved is decided explicitly and the docstring updated to match, rather than left as an undiscussed divergence from JSONLStorage.

src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_config.py (config_get) returns _KNOWN_KEYS[key]['default'], but that field was written as human-readable copy for the 'dcat config keys' table, not as a value a caller can consume.

Reproduced on the branch in a throwaway repo:
  dcat config get namespace       -> 'auto-detected  (unset — this is the default)', exit 0
  dcat config get default_storage -> '(unset)  (unset — this is the default)', exit 0

Four defects, all inside the accepted feature:

1. Values are display copy. NS=$(dcat config get namespace) yields the literal string 'auto-detected'. An unset namespace is fully supported — get_namespace falls back to detection from existing issues, then the directory name — so this hits any store that never ran 'dcat config set namespace'. The command should report what the resolution would actually produce.

2. default_storage always reports unset. It is global-only and load_config never reads the global file, so 'key not in config' is always true. A genuinely set global default_storage steering storage resolution for every repo on the machine prints '(unset)'. That is not merely unhelpful, it is the opposite of the truth.

3. The --json shape differs between paths. Set emits {key: val}; unset emits {key: null, 'set': false, 'default': '...'}, and bool defaults are stringified by str(default).lower() so .default is a string while the same key's set value is a JSON boolean. A consumer reading data['set'] raises KeyError on the set path.

4. --global is inconsistent. The global branch still exits 1 for a known-but-unset key, so 'dcat config get git_tracking' exits 0 while 'dcat config get --global git_tracking' exits 1.

List keys also change output shape: set returns a comma-joined string, unset returns '[] (show all)'.

Decision: keep exit 0 and the feature; fix the payload. Do not revert dogcat-1w21.
acceptance: An unset known key reports the value its resolution would actually produce, not table copy, and exits 0. default_storage consults the global config so a set global value is reported. The --json object has one shape for set and unset keys, with types preserved (booleans as JSON booleans, lists as lists). The --global path agrees with the local path on known-but-unset keys. An unknown key still errors with a non-zero exit. Tests cover namespace, default_storage with a global value set, a list-valued key, --global parity, and set/unset --json symmetry.

dcat git check reports green on a stale narrow .gitattributes entry
description:
GITATTRIBUTES_ENTRY in src/dogcat/constants.py widened from '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' to '.dogcats/**/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' (branch docs260809, closing dogcat-1xgi). dcat git setup appends a second merge entry instead of replacing the narrow one
description:
git_setup() in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py guards with 'if entry not in content', where entry is now the widened '.dogcats/**/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl'. An existing .gitattributes holding the old narrow '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' does not contain the new string, so setup appends, leaving two merge=dcat-jsonl lines.

Reproduced in a throwaway repo: after 'dcat git setup' on an upgraded checkout, .gitattributes holds both lines and grep -c returns 2.

tests/test_git_commands.py::TestGitSetup::test_setup_idempotent only runs setup twice from a clean repo, so it never constructs the upgrade case.

A test writes a narrow-only .gitattributes, runs setup, and asserts the file holds exactly one such line and that it is the widened pattern.

dcat git rebase rewrites issues.jsonl without the advisory lock and can crash mid-rebase
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py, the git_rebase command. Two defects.

1. No advisory lock. The command fully overwrites issues.jsonl via atomic_rewrite_jsonl with no _file_lock() anywhere in the function. A concurrent dcat append is lost outright. This directly contradicts AGENTS.md: 'Writes take an advisory lock, so concurrent dcat processes are safe.' The rglob change on branch docs260809 extends the unlocked rewrite to archive files too.

2. read_bytes() sits outside the try. The loop calls jsonl_path.read_bytes() before the try block that catches per-file errors. atomic_rewrite_jsonl creates transient tmpXXXXXX.jsonl files inside .dogcats/ during a concurrent compaction. If such a file is in the sorted(rglob(...)) snapshot but renamed away before the loop reaches it, read_bytes raises FileNotFoundError, nothing catches it, and the command dies with a traceback and no summary — while files resolved earlier in the loop are already staged by git add with no report that they were.

Both predate the branch, but rglob widens the scan to the archive directory and so widens the window for defect 2.
acceptance: git_rebase takes the store's advisory lock around the read-merge-rewrite sequence. read_bytes is inside the per-file try so a vanished file is reported as a per-file error rather than killing the command. Tests cover a file disappearing mid-loop and assert the command still reports what it resolved.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Approved scope addition: git_rebase must also warn when it skips a file that still carries conflict markers. Today a file whose parse yields empty ours and theirs is skipped silently, and if nothing else resolved, the command prints 'No JSONL conflicts found in .dogcats/' and exits 0 while the file still holds <<<<<<< markers — so the user runs 'git rebase --continue' on broken content. Keep the skip, report it, and do not let exit 0 coexist with an unresolved file. Message change, not a logic change.

dcat git rebase silently reverts dependency and link deletions under git default conflictStyle
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py _merge_three_way needs base_records to tell 'deleted by one side' apart from 'added by one side'. dcat git rebase can only populate base from a ||||||| section, which git writes only under merge.conflictStyle=diff3 or zdiff3. Git's default is 'merge', which omits the base section entirely.

So on a default git configuration, base arrives empty and _merge_three_way degrades to a plain union of both sides.

Failure scenario: branch A runs 'dcat dep X remove --depends-on Y'. Branch B edits an unrelated issue. The rebase conflicts. The user runs 'dcat git rebase' as the docs instruct, and the removed dependency is silently restored.

The command docstring says it resolves conflicts 'using the semantic merge driver logic', which promises a three-way merge the command cannot perform without the base section. Branch docs260809 leans on this prose harder than main did, since it now directs users to dcat git rebase in dcat git setup's success output and in the git guide.
acceptance: Either dcat git rebase detects a missing base section and warns that deletions cannot be honored, or it obtains the base another way (for example from the merge state in .git) so the three-way merge is real. The command docstring and the git guide stop promising three-way semantics the command cannot deliver on a default git config. A test covers a dependency deletion surviving a rebase resolution.

Add end-to-end test for merging a conflicted archive JSONL file
description:
The .gitattributes pattern was widened to '.dogcats/**/*.jsonl' so that tracked .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl files get dogcat's merge driver instead of git's default text merge, and 'dcat git rebase' switched from glob to rglob for the same reason (branch docs260809, closing dogcat-1xgi).

Neither change has an end-to-end test. Around fifteen fixtures across tests/ still write the old narrow '.dogcats/*.jsonl merge=dcat-jsonl' pattern -- test_git_commands.py, test_git_workflows.py, test_compaction_merge.py, test_git_clones.py, test_git_bisect.py, test_git_stash.py, test_git_force_push.py, test_git_server_merge_strategies.py and others -- so the suite largely exercises the configuration the widening was meant to replace.

The behaviour the widening exists to enable is therefore unverified: that a conflicted archive file is resolved by the driver rather than left with conflict markers.
acceptance: A test constructs two branches that both modify a tracked .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl, merges them with the driver installed via the widened pattern, and asserts the archive file is resolved with records from both sides and carries no conflict markers. A second test covers 'dcat git rebase' reaching an archive file through rglob. docs/merge-coverage.md gains the corresponding rows.

Dependency and link merging is not convergent: unsorted key union and side-label resolution
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py, _merge_three_way (the deps/links path). Two defects, both contradicting the convergence claim the module docstring was strengthened to make on branch docs260809.

1. The function iterates 'for key in set(base) | set(ours) | set(theirs)'. The keys are tuples of strings and Python randomizes string hashing per process, so the output order differs on every run. A reviewer confirmed three consecutive interpreter runs produce three different orders. Alice and Bob merging the same branch into the same main get semantically identical stores whose dependency and link lines are ordered differently, so their merge commits differ byte-for-byte and git later sees a whole-block text difference on those lines. No records are lost, but the churn is real and the fix is to sort the key union.

2. 'Present on both sides' resolves as merged[key] = theirs[key], picking by side label rather than by content. Two branches that both run 'dcat dep A add --depends-on B' keep whichever counterparty's created_at/created_by depending on merge direction. This is the exact divergence class dogcat-1xgi was opened for; issues and proposals were fixed there via _tie_break_key, deps and links were not.

The module docstring pre-declares defect 2 as intended in one place while the strengthened 'Deterministic and order-independent' bullet denies it, and docs/merge-coverage.md carries an unqualified green row for 'Convergent across argument order'.

Decision: fix both, rather than narrowing the claim.
acceptance: The dependency/link key union is sorted so output order is stable across processes. Both-sides resolution tie-breaks on canonical content, matching the _tie_break_key rule used for issues. A test asserts byte-identical output across repeated runs in separate processes, and a test asserts merge(base, ours, theirs) equals merge(base, theirs, ours) for deps and links. The module docstring's self-contradiction is removed and the merge-coverage row is accurate.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Approved scope addition (documentation only): the merge driver and the store now use different last-write-wins rules and neither docstring says so. merge_driver breaks an exact updated_at tie on canonical serialization; storage._parse_issue_record resolves two lines for the same issue id by file position, blind last-line-wins. If a store ever held two lines for one issue with identical updated_at and different content, 'dcat show' and the merge driver would name different winners. No realistic producer was found — datetime.now().astimezone() is microsecond-resolution and the shared-now paths compact rather than append — so this is a docstring note in both places, not a code change.

InboxStorage rewrite drops record kinds it does not model from inbox.jsonl
description:
InboxStorage._save_locked in src/dogcat/inbox.py builds the replacement file from self._proposals only. Any line in inbox.jsonl that is not a proposal is absent from the rewritten file. This is the same data-loss shape dogcat-68ij fixed for issues.jsonl, still open for the inbox.

Two kinds are affected. Event lines: already lost, and the docstring documents this as deliberate because the inbox never loads events into memory. Records whose record_type this dcat does not model: lost for no stated reason, and the merge driver now preserves exactly these through a merge, so a proposal file can carry a newer release's records into a store whose next rewrite deletes them.

The rewrite is not rare. Three call sites:
- _append when _needs_compaction is set (the corrupt-last-line repair)
- the tombstoned-proposal prune, which calls _save_locked whenever any tombstone is removed
- the namespace rename, which calls _save_locked unconditionally

So pruning proposals or renaming a namespace is enough to trigger it.

Found while verifying dogcat-68ij. The implementing agent characterised this path as running only on the corrupt-last-line repair, which is why it was left as a changelog sentence rather than a fix; the other two call sites make it routine.
acceptance: A record whose record_type InboxStorage does not model survives _save_locked, by the same preserved-bucket approach used in JSONLStorage. Tests cover a rewrite triggered by the tombstone prune and by the namespace rename. Whether event lines should also be preserved is decided explicitly and the docstring updated to match, rather than left as an undiscussed divergence from JSONLStorage.

dcat update --status tombstone bypasses the delete approval gate and makes an issue unrecoverable
description:
The --status option on create and update is a plain str with no parser or callback (src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_create.py and _cmd_update.py). create does Status(status) directly; update reaches _coerce_status in storage.py, also a bare Status(value). Both therefore accept the two sentinel members that STATUS_OPTIONS deliberately omits.

Two consequences:

1. 'dcat update <id> --status tombstone' on a live issue sets TOMBSTONE with deleted_at, deleted_by and deleted_reason all None. The tombstone guard in storage.update only fires when the issue is ALREADY tombstoned, so afterwards update, close and reopen all refuse it and the issue is unrecoverable. This reaches the absorbing tombstone without going through dcat delete, and so bypasses the confirmation AGENTS.md requires before any terminal write.

2. 'dcat create "x" --status unknown' writes "status": "unknown" into issues.jsonl — the sentinel that models.py now explicitly documents as never written by this tool.

Pre-existing behavior. docs/cli-conventions.md already records that STATUS_OPTIONS is the user-facing subset omitting tombstone and unknown, but branch docs260809 turned that into an explicit written guarantee in the Status docstring, which the CLI contradicts.
acceptance: create and update reject 'tombstone' and 'unknown' for --status with a clear error naming the allowed values, ideally by validating against STATUS_OPTIONS rather than the raw enum. Tests assert both commands exit non-zero for each sentinel. The Status docstring's claim then matches the CLI.

Two dcat archive runs in the same second overwrite the first batch, losing those issues
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_archive.py builds the destination as closed-{timestamp}.jsonl using second granularity (%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S) and does not check whether that path already exists. split_and_rewrite_jsonl then calls atomic_rewrite_jsonl, which REPLACES the archive file rather than appending to it.

Failure scenario: a script runs 'dcat archive -y' twice within the same second. The first run moves issue set A into closed-T.jsonl and removes A from issues.jsonl. The second run moves set B, and its atomic rename overwrites closed-T.jsonl with B alone. Set A is now absent from both issues.jsonl and the archive, and nothing recovers it.

_archive_inbox shares the same timestamp construction and the same exposure.

No test covers a repeated-archive case. Pre-existing, not introduced by branch docs260809.
acceptance: The archive destination cannot silently clobber an existing file — either the filename carries enough resolution to be unique, or an existing path is detected and the run appends or picks a fresh name. A test runs two archive operations against the same timestamp and asserts both batches survive.

dcat git rebase error handling: lock-timeout traceback and noisy vanished-file failure
description:
Two rough edges introduced by the dogcat-1n4x fix, both in git_rebase in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py. Approved for fixing.

1. Lock timeout raises an uncaught RuntimeError. The command now takes the store's advisory lock, which was the point of dogcat-1n4x, but on timeout (DCAT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS, 30s default) the RuntimeError escapes and the user gets a traceback. Mid-rebase is the worst moment to hand someone a stack trace, and a stale lock file is exactly when this fires. Catch it and print the remediation — advisory_file_lock's message already names the lock path and how to clear it — then exit non-zero.

2. A vanished file is reported as an error and exits 1. This followed dogcat-1n4x's acceptance criteria literally, but the realistic trigger is a transient tmpXXXX.jsonl from a concurrent compaction disappearing between the rglob snapshot and the read. That file was never the user's business and there is nothing for them to act on. Now that the command holds the lock the window is nearly closed anyway. Skip a file that no longer exists, silently. Keep the error for a file that exists but cannot be read — that is a real failure.
acceptance: A lock timeout produces a clear message naming the lock path and the remediation, with a non-zero exit and no traceback. Dependency and link merging is not convergent: unsorted key union and side-label resolution
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py, _merge_three_way (the deps/links path). Two defects, both contradicting the convergence claim the module docstring was strengthened to make on branch docs260809.

1. The function iterates 'for key in set(base) | set(ours) | set(theirs)'. The keys are tuples of strings and Python randomizes string hashing per process, so the output order differs on every run. A reviewer confirmed three consecutive interpreter runs produce three different orders. Alice and Bob merging the same branch into the same main get semantically identical stores whose dependency and link lines are ordered differently, so their merge commits differ byte-for-byte and git later sees a whole-block text difference on those lines. No records are lost, but the churn is real and the fix is to sort the key union.

2. 'Present on both sides' resolves as merged[key] = theirs[key], picking by side label rather than by content. Two branches that both run 'dcat dep A add --depends-on B' keep whichever counterparty's created_at/created_by depending on merge direction. This is the exact divergence class dogcat-1xgi was opened for; issues and proposals were fixed there via _tie_break_key, deps and links were not.

The module docstring pre-declares defect 2 as intended in one place while the strengthened 'Deterministic and order-independent' bullet denies it, and docs/merge-coverage.md carries an unqualified green row for 'Convergent across argument order'.

Decision: fix both, rather than narrowing the claim.
acceptance: The dependency/link key union is sorted so output order is stable across processes. Both-sides resolution tie-breaks on canonical content, matching the _tie_break_key rule used for issues. A test asserts byte-identical output across repeated runs in separate processes, and a test asserts merge(base, ours, theirs) equals merge(base, theirs, ours) for deps and links. The module docstring's self-contradiction is removed and the merge-coverage row is accurate.
closed_reason: Dep/link key union is sorted so output is byte-stable across processes, and both-sides records resolve through _tie_break_key instead of side label. Module docstring's self-contradiction removed; property test now compares ordered lists, which is what exposes the ordering half.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Approved scope addition (documentation only): the merge driver and the store now use different last-write-wins rules and neither docstring says so. merge_driver breaks an exact updated_at tie on canonical serialization; storage._parse_issue_record resolves two lines for the same issue id by file position, blind last-line-wins. If a store ever held two lines for one issue with identical updated_at and different content, 'dcat show' and the merge driver would name different winners. No realistic producer was found — datetime.now().astimezone() is microsecond-resolution and the shared-now paths compact rather than append — so this is a docstring note in both places, not a code change.

InboxStorage rewrite drops record kinds it does not model from inbox.jsonl
description:
InboxStorage._save_locked in src/dogcat/inbox.py builds the replacement file from self._proposals only. Any line in inbox.jsonl that is not a proposal is absent from the rewritten file. This is the same data-loss shape dogcat-68ij fixed for issues.jsonl, still open for the inbox.

Two kinds are affected. Event lines: already lost, and the docstring documents this as deliberate because the inbox never loads events into memory. Records whose record_type this dcat does not model: lost for no stated reason, and the merge driver now preserves exactly these through a merge, so a proposal file can carry a newer release's records into a store whose next rewrite deletes them.

The rewrite is not rare. Three call sites:
- _append when _needs_compaction is set (the corrupt-last-line repair)
- the tombstoned-proposal prune, which calls _save_locked whenever any tombstone is removed
- the namespace rename, which calls _save_locked unconditionally

So pruning proposals or renaming a namespace is enough to trigger it.

Found while verifying dogcat-68ij. The implementing agent characterised this path as running only on the corrupt-last-line repair, which is why it was left as a changelog sentence rather than a fix; the other two call sites make it routine.
acceptance: A record whose record_type InboxStorage does not model survives _save_locked, by the same preserved-bucket approach used in JSONLStorage. Tests cover a rewrite triggered by the tombstone prune and by the namespace rename. Whether event lines should also be preserved is decided explicitly and the docstring updated to match, rather than left as an undiscussed divergence from JSONLStorage.
closed_reason: InboxStorage now mirrors JSONLStorage: unmodelled records held in _preserved and re-emitted, events copied from the file being replaced via compact_snapshot. Event preservation was the explicit decision the issue asked for, approved by the user; pruned proposals' events go with them and namespace rename remaps event ids, both following the issue store's precedent.

dcat update --status tombstone bypasses the delete approval gate and makes an issue unrecoverable
description:
The --status option on create and update is a plain str with no parser or callback (src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_create.py and _cmd_update.py). create does Status(status) directly; update reaches _coerce_status in storage.py, also a bare Status(value). Both therefore accept the two sentinel members that STATUS_OPTIONS deliberately omits.

Two consequences:

1. 'dcat update <id> --status tombstone' on a live issue sets TOMBSTONE with deleted_at, deleted_by and deleted_reason all None. The tombstone guard in storage.update only fires when the issue is ALREADY tombstoned, so afterwards update, close and reopen all refuse it and the issue is unrecoverable. This reaches the absorbing tombstone without going through dcat delete, and so bypasses the confirmation AGENTS.md requires before any terminal write.

2. 'dcat create "x" --status unknown' writes "status": "unknown" into issues.jsonl — the sentinel that models.py now explicitly documents as never written by this tool.

Pre-existing behavior. docs/cli-conventions.md already records that STATUS_OPTIONS is the user-facing subset omitting tombstone and unknown, but branch docs260809 turned that into an explicit written guarantee in the Status docstring, which the CLI contradicts.
acceptance: create and update reject 'tombstone' and 'unknown' for --status with a clear error naming the allowed values, ideally by validating against STATUS_OPTIONS rather than the raw enum. Tests assert both commands exit non-zero for each sentinel. The Status docstring's claim then matches the CLI.
closed_reason: create and update now validate --status against STATUS_OPTIONS and name the valid values on rejection, so tombstone and unknown are no longer reachable. update validates before the per-id loop so a multi-id call rejects before any write. Tab completion already omitted the sentinels; a test pins it.

Two dcat archive runs in the same second overwrite the first batch, losing those issues
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_archive.py builds the destination as closed-{timestamp}.jsonl using second granularity (%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S) and does not check whether that path already exists. split_and_rewrite_jsonl then calls atomic_rewrite_jsonl, which REPLACES the archive file rather than appending to it.

Failure scenario: a script runs 'dcat archive -y' twice within the same second. The first run moves issue set A into closed-T.jsonl and removes A from issues.jsonl. The second run moves set B, and its atomic rename overwrites closed-T.jsonl with B alone. Set A is now absent from both issues.jsonl and the archive, and nothing recovers it.

_archive_inbox shares the same timestamp construction and the same exposure.

No test covers a repeated-archive case. Pre-existing, not introduced by branch docs260809.
acceptance: The archive destination cannot silently clobber an existing file — either the filename carries enough resolution to be unique, or an existing path is detected and the run appends or picks a fresh name. A test runs two archive operations against the same timestamp and asserts both batches survive.
closed_reason: Archive destination is claimed with O_EXCL and falls back to closed-<ts>-2.jsonl, -3 and so on, for both the issue and inbox archives. Numeric suffix chosen over sub-second resolution so two branches archiving the same batch produce one filename the merge driver can union. Empty reservations are removed.

dcat git setup rewrites .gitattributes line endings from CRLF to LF
description:
_install_gitattributes_entry in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py rebuilds the file with content.splitlines() and then '\n'.join(kept) + '\n'. splitlines() strips both \r\n and \n, so the rejoin emits LF regardless of what the file used.

On the 'replaced' path — the one that fires when a pre-widening dogcat entry is rewritten in place (dogcat-12v8) — a .gitattributes written with CRLF comes back entirely LF. The user sees a whole-file diff where they expected a one-line change, and a reviewer on their PR sees the same.

The other two paths are safe: 'added' appends to the original content untouched, and 'present' returns content unchanged. So this only bites a checkout that actually carries a legacy entry, once, on upgrade.

Low severity — dogcat is POSIX-targeted and git normalizes endings on checkout under common configurations (see dogcat-69vm for the wider non-POSIX gap). But the fix is contained and the symptom is confusing out of proportion to the cause.
acceptance: A .gitattributes using CRLF keeps CRLF after dcat git setup rewrites a legacy entry, and one using LF keeps LF. The only changed line is the entry itself. A test covers both endings on the replaced path, and confirms the added and present paths still leave content byte-identical apart from the intended append.

TUI storage mutations block the Textual event loop
description: Issue save (src/dogcat/tui/detail_panel.py:955 via action_save), delete (tui/dashboard.py:543), and refresh/reload (dashboard.py:569-570) call storage.update/delete/reload synchronously on the Textual event loop - no @work(thread=True), run_worker, or to_thread anywhere under src/dogcat/tui/. The write path takes the advisory flock with a 50ms poll loop bounded at 30s (locking.py), then fsyncs, and can pay a git subprocess plus a full-file compaction rewrite inside the same call. When an agent CLI process holds the lock (the prescribed concurrent workflow), the TUI freezes - no repaint, no keystrokes - for up to the lock timeout. Fix: run storage mutations and reload in a Textual thread worker and post Saved/Cancelled results back as messages; the storage layer is already process-safe via the flock.

Split the shared .issues.lock into per-file locks
description: One LOCK_FILENAME (src/dogcat/constants.py:304) serializes writers of independent files: issues.jsonl (storage.py:391), inbox.jsonl (inbox.py:160), the event log (event_log.py:277), the web namespace pin (web/propose/routes.py:93), and dcat git rebase (_cmd_docs.py:580, deliberately whole-store). A web proposal submit queues behind an issues.jsonl compaction/archive - files it never touches - polling 50ms up to 30s, then errors. Fix: per-file lock paths (.issues.lock / .inbox.lock), keeping a shared or dual-lock scheme only for operations that genuinely need cross-file atomicity (the rebase resolve). Do not weaken any locking guarantee - this narrows scope, never removes a lock.

Strip all trailing punctuation, not just ':', from issue IDs during resolution
description: dogcat-1zhb made 'dcat show dogcat-1iw8:' resolve by rstripping ':' in resolve_partial_id() (src/dogcat/_id_resolve.py:47), but an ID pasted out of prose or a terminal pane can carry other trailing punctuation: 'dcat show dogcat-1iw8.' and 'dcat show dogcat-1iw8,' still fail with not-found. Issue IDs are base36 (0-9a-z, see _base36_encode in src/dogcat/idgen.py) joined to a namespace by hyphens, so no legitimate ID ends in punctuation and stripping it cannot shadow a real match. Fix: widen the rstrip in resolve_partial_id to a shared set of trailing punctuation — : . , ; ! ? ) ] } ' and double-quote — covering issues and proposals in every command that resolves an ID.
acceptance: 'dcat show <id>X' resolves the same as 'dcat show <id>' for each stripped character; a bare punctuation-only argument still resolves to None; a LEADING punctuation character is still not stripped and does not match; tests in tests/test_id_resolve.py cover each case; CHANGELOG.md gets a Fixed entry under [Unreleased].

description: src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_chart.py:11-12 imports rich.console and rich.text at module scope. Because cli/__init__.py eagerly imports all command modules, every dcat invocation pays the rich import; measured at ~278ms of the ~605ms total import dogcat.cli (pyproject.toml PLC0415 rationale documents the deferred-import doctrine this violates). Only dcat chart needs rich. Fix: move both imports into the chart-rendering functions, matching the pattern _formatting.py already uses.

Cache git walkup boundary and merged config per process
description: get_rc_walkup_boundary (src/dogcat/config.py:90) forks git rev-parse --show-toplevel on every call and load_config (config.py:471) re-parses the same 2-3 TOML files on every call. One plain dcat list reaches them 4-5 times (call sites: cli/_helpers.py:276, config.py:442/826/830/845, cli/_cmd_read.py:539); tab completion pays 3-4 git forks per Tab press. Fix: functools.cache on get_rc_walkup_boundary/_find_rc_parent keyed on the resolved start dir (precedent: the _is_default_branch per-instance memo in storage.py), plus a per-process DogcatConfig memo keyed on dogcats_dir, cleared by save_config/save_local_config/set_namespace. Long-running TUI/web callers should key on (mtime, size) like _refresh_inbox_if_stale in web/propose/routes.py:175. Also consider computing the boundary lazily in walkup_find_store when cwd/.dogcats exists, and folding in the git config user.email fork (_helpers.py:227). Flagged independently by io-batching, caching-wins, and startup lenses.
acceptance: a single dcat list spawns git rev-parse at most once and parses each config file at most once; config writes invalidate the memo; TUI/web pick up config edits; tests pass

description: StreamWatcher.events (src/dogcat/stream.py:536) gets an append per observed store mutation in _handle_event (:573) and nothing ever reads or trims it - the only reader in the tree is a test asserting it is a list. Each entry carries a full per-field changes dict. In the long-running dcat stream process this is unbounded heap growth for the process lifetime: an agent-heavy setup that leaves stream running for days retains every event payload for no consumer. Fix: delete the append (the streaming path already prints each event immediately), or bound it with collections.deque(maxlen=N) if tests want a recent-events window.
acceptance: no unbounded collection in StreamWatcher; stream output unchanged; test_stream.py updated and passing

Fix: check record_type via the EVENT_LINE_PREFIX fast-path and the raw issue_id field before deserializing; apply limit during the scan (or iterate from the tail for newest-first); drop the unneeded get_storage load. Flagged by allocations and payloads.

TUI storage mutations block the Textual event loop
description: Issue save (src/dogcat/tui/detail_panel.py:955 via action_save), delete (tui/dashboard.py:543), and refresh/reload (dashboard.py:569-570) call storage.update/delete/reload synchronously on the Textual event loop - no @work(thread=True), run_worker, or to_thread anywhere under src/dogcat/tui/. The write path takes the advisory flock with a 50ms poll loop bounded at 30s (locking.py), then fsyncs, and can pay a git subprocess plus a full-file compaction rewrite inside the same call. When an agent CLI process holds the lock (the prescribed concurrent workflow), the TUI freezes - no repaint, no keystrokes - for up to the lock timeout. Fix: run storage mutations and reload in a Textual thread worker and post Saved/Cancelled results back as messages; the storage layer is already process-safe via the flock.
acceptance: TUI stays responsive during a contended save (verify with a test holding the lock); save/delete/refresh behavior unchanged; TUI tests pass

append_jsonl_payload does 4 filesystem operations per append
description: src/dogcat/_jsonl_io.py:100-109: each append does exists() + stat() + a separate open/seek/read(1) trailing-newline probe + the open(ab)/write/fsync. One open(ab) handle can answer all of it: f.tell() gives the empty/size check and a same-fd seek-back read gives the newline probe. Runs on every store mutation (batched multi-id writes already pay it once via batch()). The fsync dominates and is a deliberate durability choice - keep it; this trims only the redundant syscalls around it.
acceptance: append semantics (newline handling, empty-file case, fsync) unchanged; storage tests pass

Stream watcher diffs the entire store on every filesystem event
description: The incremental parser in dcat stream already extracts which issue IDs the newly appended bytes touched, but _compute_diff (src/dogcat/stream.py:109-200) then compares every field of every issue in old vs new state anyway, plus a full dict copy of current_state (:239); the inbox emitter twins the pattern (:352, :438). The per-record dict_to_issue -> issue_to_dict round trip (:257-258, :290, :101) adds construct-then-reserialize cost per line and per full reload. Runs per store-write FS event for the process lifetime, often multiple events per atomic write. Fix: diff only the IDs the incremental parse touched, keeping the full diff for the _full_reload path (compaction) where it is genuinely needed; consider diffing on normalized raw dicts to skip the construction round trip. description: The completers in src/dogcat/cli/_completions.py (complete_issue_ids and siblings at :54, label/owner/namespace completers, plus get_namespaces in storage.py) iterate storage.list(), which forces dict_to_issue on every record - datetime parses, enum coercions, comment lists - the cost _lazy_issues.py documents as ~40% of load wall time at scale. Completion reads only full_id, status, namespace, title, labels, owner, all present on the raw parsed dicts LazyIssueMap already holds. This runs per Tab press in a fresh process, the most latency-sensitive path in the tool. Fix: add a raw-field iterator on LazyIssueMap (sibling of iter_id_parent) and use it in all completers. Optional follow-on from the caching-wins lens: persist completion tuples to the existing ~/.cache/dogcat/<key>/ dir keyed on (issues.jsonl mtime, size), falling back to a full load on mismatch. Flagged by 4 of 7 lenses.

resolve_partial_id builds an O(n) key set on every resolve
description: src/dogcat/_id_resolve.py:52 copies all issue keys into a fresh set before the exact-match check, so every storage.get/resolve_id call (storage.py:740,759) pays O(n) even when the argument is a full ID that LazyIssueMap.__contains__ answers in O(1) - and internal references are almost always full IDs. Multi-id commands (dcat close A B C) pay one set per argument; on show-all this stacks with the blocked-map rebuild (dogcat-6cjx) into a second quadratic term. Fix: test partial_id in ids via the mapping first; build the candidate set only for the suffix-fallback scan. Exact match already wins first, so no semantics change. Flagged by hot-loops and allocations.
acceptance: exact-ID resolves do no O(n) copy; partial-suffix resolution behavior unchanged; id-resolution tests pass

title: resolve_partial_id builds an O(n) key set on every resolve
Split the shared .issues.lock into per-file locks
description: One LOCK_FILENAME (src/dogcat/constants.py:304) serializes writers of independent files: issues.jsonl (storage.py:391), inbox.jsonl (inbox.py:160), the event log (event_log.py:277), the web namespace pin (web/propose/routes.py:93), and dcat git rebase (_cmd_docs.py:580, deliberately whole-store). A web proposal submit queues behind an issues.jsonl compaction/archive - files it never touches - polling 50ms up to 30s, then errors. Fix: per-file lock paths (.issues.lock / .inbox.lock), keeping a shared or dual-lock scheme only for operations that genuinely need cross-file atomicity (the rebase resolve). Do not weaken any locking guarantee - this narrows scope, never removes a lock.
acceptance: inbox and issues writers no longer contend; whole-store operations still exclude both; concurrent-write tests pass
