Read-only design pass (2026-08-10). Deferred by maintainer decision: gain is bounded, cost touches a data-integrity guarantee.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE TEXT: the event log is NOT an independent file. _BaseEventLog.filename resolves to issues.jsonl for EventLog (event_log.py:313-316) and inbox.jsonl for InboxEventLog (event_log.py:319-320). Two callers append events standalone via try_emit -> append (storage.py:1141 change_namespace, storage.py:1236 rename_namespace), both writing into issues.jsonl. Giving the event log its own lock file lets those appends interleave with _save_locked's atomic_rewrite_jsonl (storage.py:521) and be silently dropped. Any split must key on the TARGET DATA FILE, not on the class. Also: event_log.py:128-130 has a comment stating the lock is shared across both logs, stale once this lands.

Proposed layout: .issues.lock (JSONLStorage._file_lock storage.py:458, EventLog, storage.archive storage.py:1751); .inbox.lock (InboxStorage._file_lock inbox.py:158, InboxEventLog, _archive_inbox _cmd_archive.py:115); .config.lock (web namespace pin routes.py:93, which writes only config.local.toml and touches no JSONL). archive/*.jsonl needs no lock of its own - every writer already holds the lock of the file it drains. Acquisition order issues -> inbox -> config, released reverse.

Whole-store exclusion: _cmd_docs.py:578 (dcat git rebase) is already an ExitStack; enter issues then inbox into it, via a store_lock_paths(dogcats_dir) registry helper so a future fourth store file cannot silently lose rebase protection. Both acquisitions must stay inside the existing try at _cmd_docs.py:581-587 or a timeout escapes as a traceback and breaks test_lock_timeout_is_reported_not_raised.

Pairs that look like they need cross-file atomicity and do not: dcat archive (_cmd_archive.py:269 then :272) and dcat repair-jsonl (_cmd_admin.py:744 then :747) already take two sequential, never-nested acquisitions; dcat inbox accept uses an application-level compensating rollback (_cmd_inbox.py:472-513).

TWO BLOCKERS that must land with the change:
1. .gitignore:12 has exactly one entry, .dogcats/.issues.lock, and dcat init writes that single line (_cmd_init.py:201); the doctor check accepts .issues.lock or .dogcats/ (_cmd_docs.py:341-346). New lock files would land untracked-and-unignored in every existing checkout. Switch all three to .dogcats/*.lock.
2. Mixed-version window: an old dcat locking inbox.jsonl under .issues.lock and a new dcat locking it under .inbox.lock stop excluding each other. Narrow (one store, two dcat versions, concurrent writes) but it weakens a guarantee this issue says never to weaken. Belongs in a CHANGELOG upgrade note.

REQUIRED TEST, the one this must not land without: hold .issues.lock, assert EventLog(dogcats_dir).append() still times out; hold .inbox.lock, assert InboxEventLog append times out. Without it, a wrong split passes every other test and corrupts issues.jsonl under compaction. Plus: non-contention proof (hold .issues.lock, DCAT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS=0.2, InboxStorage.create_proposal completes - times out today); same-file contention preserved both directions; parameterize _store_lock_held (tests/test_git_rebase.py:61-87) over the lock name and run test_waits_for_the_store_lock (:341) and test_lock_timeout_is_reported_not_raised (:365) against both; add the _archive_inbox mirror of tests/test_archive.py:835, which has no such test today; update docs/merge-coverage.md:97, whose row claims the resolve runs under the store lock, singular.

Why deferred: docs/web-ui.md:37-41 describes the propose server as local, single-worker and unauthenticated, so the stall this issue describes needs a web submit to overlap a compaction or archive on the same checkout.

title: Split the shared .issues.lock into per-file locks
description: One LOCK_FILENAME (src/dogcat/constants.py:304) serializes writers of independent files: issues.jsonl (storage.py:391), inbox.jsonl (inbox.py:160), the event log (event_log.py:277), the web namespace pin (web/propose/routes.py:93), and dcat git rebase (_cmd_docs.py:580, deliberately whole-store). A web proposal submit queues behind an issues.jsonl compaction/archive - files it never touches - polling 50ms up to 30s, then errors. Fix: per-file lock paths (.issues.lock / .inbox.lock), keeping a shared or dual-lock scheme only for operations that genuinely need cross-file atomicity (the rebase resolve). Do not weaken any locking guarantee - this narrows scope, never removes a lock.
acceptance: inbox and issues writers no longer contend; whole-store operations still exclude both; concurrent-write tests pass

Cross-process parse cache for the loaded store
description: Every dcat invocation re-reads and re-parses issues.jsonl from scratch (JSONLStorage._load, src/dogcat/storage.py:242); nothing persists across processes. Small today (742 lines / ~130KB) - LazyIssueMap and the event-line fast path already blunt it - so this is a scale play, not urgent: the review rated it worth doing at the store sizes dogcat-2my1 anticipates. Fix sketch: persist a compact snapshot to the existing ~/.cache/dogcat/<project_key>/ dir keyed on (issues.jsonl mtime, size) or a content hash; any mismatch falls back to the normal load, so correctness never depends on the cache. Measure with benchmark.py before/after (relates dogcat-5tdx).
acceptance: cache hit skips the full parse with identical resulting state; stale/missing cache falls back cleanly; benchmark numbers recorded

Fix: a non-materializing emptiness check (len of the id map, or a small storage.is_empty() helper).
acceptance: empty-store vs empty-view messaging unchanged; no Issue construction on the check; tests pass

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Deferred 2026-08-11 while the other 24 children of dogcat-2z9f landed. Not started; no code exists for it.

Reason: every other child was a local fix whose worst case is a slower command. This one adds a persistent artifact outside the repo, and its staleness logic is the only thing between a cache hit and wrong issue state. At 742 lines / ~130KB the payoff does not justify carrying that risk yet, which matches this issue's own framing as a scale play.

Two things landed that change the baseline and should be re-measured before this is picked up: LazyIssueMap now serves completion and namespace counts from raw dicts without constructing Issue objects (dogcat-4qif), and storage.is_empty() removed the last full materialization on the list empty-result path (dogcat-1ot9). Re-measure with benchmark.py before assuming the parse cost is still where the review found it.

When picked up: write the stale-cache and corrupt-cache fallback tests first. Correctness must never depend on the cache - any mismatch on (mtime, size) or content hash falls back to a full load. Note that mtime+size alone cannot detect a same-size in-place edit within one filesystem timestamp tick; decide explicitly whether that matters for a store the merge driver rewrites.

Children are tiered by the review: priority 1 = Red (fix now), priority 2 = Yellow (should address), priority 3 = Green (fix when nearby). title: Move module-scope rich imports in _cmd_chart.py into functions
description: src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_chart.py:11-12 imports rich.console and rich.text at module scope. Because cli/__init__.py eagerly imports all command modules, every dcat invocation pays the rich import; measured at ~278ms of the ~605ms total import dogcat.cli (pyproject.toml PLC0415 rationale documents the deferred-import doctrine this violates). Only dcat chart needs rich. Fix: move both imports into the chart-rendering functions, matching the pattern _formatting.py already uses.
acceptance: rich no longer imports on a plain dcat list (verify with python -X importtime); dcat chart still renders; tests pass

Cache git walkup boundary and merged config per process
description: get_rc_walkup_boundary (src/dogcat/config.py:90) forks git rev-parse --show-toplevel on every call and load_config (config.py:471) re-parses the same 2-3 TOML files on every call. One plain dcat list reaches them 4-5 times (call sites: cli/_helpers.py:276, config.py:442/826/830/845, cli/_cmd_read.py:539); tab completion pays 3-4 git forks per Tab press. Fix: functools.cache on get_rc_walkup_boundary/_find_rc_parent keyed on the resolved start dir (precedent: the _is_default_branch per-instance memo in storage.py), plus a per-process DogcatConfig memo keyed on dogcats_dir, cleared by save_config/save_local_config/set_namespace. Long-running TUI/web callers should key on (mtime, size) like _refresh_inbox_if_stale in web/propose/routes.py:175. Also consider computing the boundary lazily in walkup_find_store when cwd/.dogcats exists, and folding in the git config user.email fork (_helpers.py:227). Flagged independently by io-batching, caching-wins, and startup lenses.
acceptance: a single dcat list spawns git rev-parse at most once and parses each config file at most once; config writes invalidate the memo; TUI/web pick up config edits; tests pass

dcat stream accumulates StreamEvents in a list that is never read
description: StreamWatcher.events (src/dogcat/stream.py:536) gets an append per observed store mutation in _handle_event (:573) and nothing ever reads or trims it - the only reader in the tree is a test asserting it is a list. Each entry carries a full per-field changes dict. In the long-running dcat stream process this is unbounded heap growth for the process lifetime: an agent-heavy setup that leaves stream running for days retains every event payload for no consumer. Fix: delete the append (the streaming path already prints each event immediately), or bound it with collections.deque(maxlen=N) if tests want a recent-events window.
acceptance: no unbounded collection in StreamWatcher; stream output unchanged; test_stream.py updated and passing
closed_reason: Implemented and verified: full suite 3354 passed, just lint-all clean

TUI storage mutations block the Textual event loop
description: Issue save (src/dogcat/tui/detail_panel.py:955 via action_save), delete (tui/dashboard.py:543), and refresh/reload (dashboard.py:569-570) call storage.update/delete/reload synchronously on the Textual event loop - no @work(thread=True), run_worker, or to_thread anywhere under src/dogcat/tui/. The write path takes the advisory flock with a 50ms poll loop bounded at 30s (locking.py), then fsyncs, and can pay a git subprocess plus a full-file compaction rewrite inside the same call. When an agent CLI process holds the lock (the prescribed concurrent workflow), the TUI freezes - no repaint, no keystrokes - for up to the lock timeout. Fix: run storage mutations and reload in a Textual thread worker and post Saved/Cancelled results back as messages; the storage layer is already process-safe via the flock.
acceptance: TUI stays responsive during a contended save (verify with a test holding the lock); save/delete/refresh behavior unchanged; TUI tests pass
closed_reason: Implemented and verified: full suite 3354 passed, just lint-all clean

title: TUI storage mutations block the Textual event loop
Tab completion: read raw dicts instead of materializing Issue objects
description: The completers in src/dogcat/cli/_completions.py (complete_issue_ids and siblings at :54, label/owner/namespace completers, plus get_namespaces in storage.py) iterate storage.list(), which forces dict_to_issue on every record - datetime parses, enum coercions, comment lists - the cost _lazy_issues.py documents as ~40% of load wall time at scale. Completion reads only full_id, status, namespace, title, labels, owner, all present on the raw parsed dicts LazyIssueMap already holds. This runs per Tab press in a fresh process, the most latency-sensitive path in the tool. Fix: add a raw-field iterator on LazyIssueMap (sibling of iter_id_parent) and use it in all completers. Optional follow-on from the caching-wins lens: persist completion tuples to the existing ~/.cache/dogcat/<key>/ dir keyed on (issues.jsonl mtime, size), falling back to a full load on mismatch. Flagged by 4 of 7 lenses.
acceptance: completers produce identical output without constructing Issue objects; completion tests pass
closed_reason: Implemented and verified: full suite 3354 passed, just lint-all clean

title: Tab completion: read raw dicts instead of materializing Issue objects
Stream watcher diffs the entire store on every filesystem event
description: The incremental parser in dcat stream already extracts which issue IDs the newly appended bytes touched, but _compute_diff (src/dogcat/stream.py:109-200) then compares every field of every issue in old vs new state anyway, plus a full dict copy of current_state (:239); the inbox emitter twins the pattern (:352, :438). The per-record dict_to_issue -> issue_to_dict round trip (:257-258, :290, :101) adds construct-then-reserialize cost per line and per full reload. Runs per store-write FS event for the process lifetime, often multiple events per atomic write. Fix: diff only the IDs the incremental parse touched, keeping the full diff for the _full_reload path (compaction) where it is genuinely needed; consider diffing on normalized raw dicts to skip the construction round trip. Flagged by hot-loops and allocations.
acceptance: per-event work scales with changed records, not store size; emitted events unchanged; stream tests pass
closed_reason: Implemented and verified: full suite 3354 passed, just lint-all clean

title: Stream watcher diffs the entire store on every filesystem event
append_jsonl_payload does 4 filesystem operations per append
description: src/dogcat/_jsonl_io.py:100-109: each append does exists() + stat() + a separate open/seek/read(1) trailing-newline probe + the open(ab)/write/fsync. One open(ab) handle can answer all of it: f.tell() gives the empty/size check and a same-fd seek-back read gives the newline probe. Runs on every store mutation (batched multi-id writes already pay it once via batch()). The fsync dominates and is a deliberate durability choice - keep it; this trims only the redundant syscalls around it.
acceptance: append semantics (newline handling, empty-file case, fsync) unchanged; storage tests pass
closed_reason: Implemented and verified: full suite 3354 passed, just lint-all clean

Largely absorbed by the config memo in dogcat-2s9r if that lands first.

resolve_partial_id builds an O(n) key set on every resolve
description: src/dogcat/_id_resolve.py:52 copies all issue keys into a fresh set before the exact-match check, so every storage.get/resolve_id call (storage.py:740,759) pays O(n) even when the argument is a full ID that LazyIssueMap.__contains__ answers in O(1) - and internal references are almost always full IDs. Multi-id commands (dcat close A B C) pay one set per argument; on show-all this stacks with the blocked-map rebuild (dogcat-6cjx) into a second quadratic term. Fix: test partial_id in ids via the mapping first; build the candidate set only for the suffix-fallback scan. Exact match already wins first, so no semantics change. Flagged by hot-loops and allocations.
acceptance: exact-ID resolves do no O(n) copy; partial-suffix resolution behavior unchanged; id-resolution tests pass

title: resolve_partial_id builds an O(n) key set on every resolve
Move the default-branch git check outside the store write lock
description: Inside JSONLStorage._append (src/dogcat/storage.py:487-497), the compaction gate calls _is_default_branch() while holding the file lock; the first call per instance forks git rev-parse (10s timeout, possibly a second fork for init.defaultBranch), extending lock hold for every waiter (50ms polls, 30s abort). The memo docstring itself says the branch cannot legitimately change mid-command, so warming it before acquiring the lock is semantics-preserving; only the line-count check and the rewrite need the lock. Overlaps dogcat-2my1 only on the rewrite cost itself, which stays tracked there.
acceptance: no subprocess runs inside the file lock on the append path; compaction still triggers only on the default branch; tests pass

description: _render_issue_show (src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_read.py:447, reached via :400 and show-all at :881) calls deps.get_blocked_issues(storage) for every rendered issue that has children; that helper (deps.py:125) materializes every issue in the store plus a full dependency map to annotate a handful of child rows. show-all repeats the rebuild per issue, scaling toward O(n_store^2). description: merge_jsonl and its helpers (src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:450-579) re-run classify_record per record across ~10 separate passes: _merge_issues_lww/_merge_proposals/_merge_events/_merge_unknown each build and iterate [*ours, *theirs], plus 6 _replay_with_ops passes and per-record orjson.dumps(OPT_SORT_KEYS) tie-break keys. Cold path (per divergent merge) and currently well within the test_merge_scale.py budgets - this is headroom. Fix: one bucketing pass into per-kind lists fed to each merger; itertools.chain instead of combined lists; memoize the tie-break serialization within one merge call (id-keyed, since dicts are unhashable). Only pursue with before/after numbers from test_merge_scale.py (relates dogcat-5tdx). Flagged by hot-loops, allocations, and caching-wins.
acceptance: merge output byte-identical on the existing merge test corpus; scale-test timings not worse

title: Performance improvements from perf-cop review
Split the shared .issues.lock into per-file locks
description: One LOCK_FILENAME (src/dogcat/constants.py:304) serializes writers of independent files: issues.jsonl (storage.py:391), inbox.jsonl (inbox.py:160), the event log (event_log.py:277), the web namespace pin (web/propose/routes.py:93), and dcat git rebase (_cmd_docs.py:580, deliberately whole-store). A web proposal submit queues behind an issues.jsonl compaction/archive - files it never touches - polling 50ms up to 30s, then errors. Fix: per-file lock paths (.issues.lock / .inbox.lock), keeping a shared or dual-lock scheme only for operations that genuinely need cross-file atomicity (the rebase resolve). Do not weaken any locking guarantee - this narrows scope, never removes a lock.
acceptance: inbox and issues writers no longer contend; whole-store operations still exclude both; concurrent-write tests pass

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Read-only design pass (2026-08-10). Deferred by maintainer decision: gain is bounded, cost touches a data-integrity guarantee.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE TEXT: the event log is NOT an independent file. _BaseEventLog.filename resolves to issues.jsonl for EventLog (event_log.py:313-316) and inbox.jsonl for InboxEventLog (event_log.py:319-320). Two callers append events standalone via try_emit -> append (storage.py:1141 change_namespace, storage.py:1236 rename_namespace), both writing into issues.jsonl. Giving the event log its own lock file lets those appends interleave with _save_locked's atomic_rewrite_jsonl (storage.py:521) and be silently dropped. Any split must key on the TARGET DATA FILE, not on the class. Also: event_log.py:128-130 has a comment stating the lock is shared across both logs, stale once this lands.

Proposed layout: .issues.lock (JSONLStorage._file_lock storage.py:458, EventLog, storage.archive storage.py:1751); .inbox.lock (InboxStorage._file_lock inbox.py:158, InboxEventLog, _archive_inbox _cmd_archive.py:115); .config.lock (web namespace pin routes.py:93, which writes only config.local.toml and touches no JSONL). archive/*.jsonl needs no lock of its own - every writer already holds the lock of the file it drains. Acquisition order issues -> inbox -> config, released reverse.

Whole-store exclusion: _cmd_docs.py:578 (dcat git rebase) is already an ExitStack; enter issues then inbox into it, via a store_lock_paths(dogcats_dir) registry helper so a future fourth store file cannot silently lose rebase protection. Both acquisitions must stay inside the existing try at _cmd_docs.py:581-587 or a timeout escapes as a traceback and breaks test_lock_timeout_is_reported_not_raised.

Pairs that look like they need cross-file atomicity and do not: dcat archive (_cmd_archive.py:269 then :272) and dcat repair-jsonl (_cmd_admin.py:744 then :747) already take two sequential, never-nested acquisitions; dcat inbox accept uses an application-level compensating rollback (_cmd_inbox.py:472-513).

TWO BLOCKERS that must land with the change:
1. .gitignore:12 has exactly one entry, .dogcats/.issues.lock, and dcat init writes that single line (_cmd_init.py:201); the doctor check accepts .issues.lock or .dogcats/ (_cmd_docs.py:341-346). New lock files would land untracked-and-unignored in every existing checkout. Switch all three to .dogcats/*.lock.
2. Mixed-version window: an old dcat locking inbox.jsonl under .issues.lock and a new dcat locking it under .inbox.lock stop excluding each other. Narrow (one store, two dcat versions, concurrent writes) but it weakens a guarantee this issue says never to weaken. Belongs in a CHANGELOG upgrade note.

REQUIRED TEST, the one this must not land without: hold .issues.lock, assert EventLog(dogcats_dir).append() still times out; hold .inbox.lock, assert InboxEventLog append times out. Without it, a wrong split passes every other test and corrupts issues.jsonl under compaction. Plus: non-contention proof (hold .issues.lock, DCAT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS=0.2, InboxStorage.create_proposal completes - times out today); same-file contention preserved both directions; parameterize _store_lock_held (tests/test_git_rebase.py:61-87) over the lock name and run test_waits_for_the_store_lock (:341) and test_lock_timeout_is_reported_not_raised (:365) against both; add the _archive_inbox mirror of tests/test_archive.py:835, which has no such test today; update docs/merge-coverage.md:97, whose row claims the resolve runs under the store lock, singular.

Why deferred: docs/web-ui.md:37-41 describes the propose server as local, single-worker and unauthenticated, so the stall this issue describes needs a web submit to overlap a compaction or archive on the same checkout.

title: publish.yml lint step fails: pnpm not installed in publish job
description:
The Publish Release workflow (.github/workflows/publish.yml) runs 'uvx --from rust-just just lint-all', but the publish job never installs node/pnpm. 'just lint' shells out to pnpm for oxfmt, oxlint and stylelint, so the step dies with:

    sh: 1: pnpm: not found (x3)
    error: recipe `lint` failed on line 35 with exit code 1
    error: recipe `lint-all` failed on line 43 with exit code 1

Commit 1ab3b7b ('Install pnpm and node deps in CI before lint', dogcat-1haz) added the 'Install pnpm' (pnpm/action-setup v6.0.10, version 11) and 'Install node dependencies' (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile) steps to .github/workflows/ci.yml only, and missed publish.yml. v0.13.1 was released before pnpm entered 'just lint', so v0.14.0 is the first release to hit this.

Impact: PR #34 (release/v0.14.0) merged as b354d99, run 31513685850 failed at Lint, and none of the downstream work happened — no v0.14.0 tag, no GitHub release, no PyPI upload, no Homebrew formula bump. Only v0.14.0-rc.1 exists.

Fix: add the same two steps to the publish job in .github/workflows/publish.yml, immediately before the Lint step, using the same pinned action SHA as ci.yml.
acceptance: publish.yml's publish job installs pnpm and runs 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile' before 'just lint-all', matching ci.yml; the v0.14.0 publish run reaches the Test step and completes, producing the v0.14.0 tag, GitHub release, PyPI upload and Homebrew bump.
